title: The fifth week
subtitle: The six-week visit is next week. Write your questions down now, while you remember them.

baby.development: Your baby is cooing back at you and may smile in response to a face rather than by accident. They are awake for longer and sleep in slightly longer stretches at night.

you.body: Bleeding should be spotting or finished. If you are breastfeeding, your period may not return for months, and that is not a reliable sign of anything.
you.mind: Sleep deprivation builds. If you are snapping at people or crying at small things, that is the sleep talking, and it is also worth mentioning at the visit.

coreActions.title: Book the six-week postpartum visit
coreActions.why: This is the visit that clears you for exercise, checks the wound and the pelvic floor, and covers contraception.
coreActions.detail: Ask for a pelvic floor check, not just a look at the wound. Ask what exercise is safe to start and what to wait on. Ask about contraception you actually want, including options that do not affect milk supply.

coreActions.title: Know when bleeding is not normal anymore
coreActions.why: Bleeding that was tapering and then gets heavier is the pattern worth calling about.
coreActions.detail: Spotting that comes and goes for six weeks is common. Bleeding that fills a pad in an hour, passes large clots, or comes back heavy after it had stopped is not.

coreActions.title: Walk outside once a day
coreActions.why: Daylight and gentle movement do more for mood in the first months than almost anything else you can do alone.
coreActions.detail: Ten minutes is enough. Go at a time when someone else can hold the baby, or take the baby. It is not exercise, it is a change of scene.

alsoKnow.title: Your period may be months away
alsoKnow.body: If you are breastfeeding, the first period often does not return until feeds drop. That does not mean you cannot get pregnant, and it is not a contraception method.

alsoKnow.title: A carrier buys you two hands
alsoKnow.body: A soft structured carrier or a wrap lets you eat, walk, and answer a door. Look for one that holds the baby high and tight, with the head clear and the chin off the chest.

redFlags.text: Bleeding that soaks a pad in an hour, or bleeding that returns heavy after stopping
Pain or swelling in one calf
Feeling hopeless, or thoughts of harming yourself or the baby
